title: Resolve upstream ref helper binding contradiction; upstream bead write denied
description:
Spec blocker at Bennett ISA 0.9 §11.1/K19: consumers reject unbound names and there are no implicit bindings/defaults, but published ref@0.9 qxor(parameters:[N]) reads free s/t, and bind.value.add(N,a,b,t) invokes value.add with args:[N] while value.add(parameters:[N]) reads free a/b/t. A strictly lexical typed invoke cannot instantiate these records. Proposed exact text after K19 positional invoke: "A named recipe body is closed over its declared parameters and its own lexical declarations; invoke does not inherit caller bindings except through explicit actuals. Every recipe in the bound library MUST satisfy this closure condition." Add complete ordered typed free-variable interfaces to each helper and explicit corresponding invoke actuals, regenerate catalog/hash/fixtures, and add a closed-binding vector. An alternative retaining the catalog hash requires an explicit binding rule for existing free variables, never a guessed caller-environment fallback.

Required upstream filing attempted via bd create in bennett-isa-spec. Exact error: failed to open database: embeddeddolt: init schema: embeddeddolt: open db: failed to load database "b_isa_spec": openat LOCK: read-only file system. No upstream file changed. Transfer this issue to bennett-isa-spec when writable. This is a contract decision, not a scope reduction; implement independently specified paths meanwhile.

title: Finish and independently verify remaining ISA 0.9 conformance vectors
description: Conformance audit currently inventories all 519 ISA repository cases (A22/B35/C340/D13/E38/F37/G24/H10), ten §16.3 example objects and four accepted portable manifests (23 source vectors). Source/cost tests directly replay selected target/AST/aggregation fixtures, equivalent witnesses cover other §11 properties, and the controlled-action full basis trace agrees with the published reference binary using its explicit 0.8 compatibility object. No full-conformance pass is claimed. Remaining per-vector coverage is recorded by scripts/conformance.py and docs/conformance-report.json; --require-complete exits 2 while any vector is unexercised. Installed reference 0.9 admission probe: check controlled-action-09/controlled.bisa exits 1, stderr: §1: expected isa=0.8. It cannot independently consume a 0.9 schedule. After ref helper binding is specified (bennett-sched-enz), complete all source builders/cleanup/placement/claims and replay every remaining relevant normative and portable vector; distinguish direct replay, semantic compatibility evidence and staged checks. Run own pre-push gate; never a full sibling gate. Runner owns commits.
notes: Additional resource corner case to determine/replay explicitly: resources::aggregate currently omits zero-duration live intervals from the peak sweep while allocator capacity counts instantaneous live demands. Validate zero-duration gates/allocation lifetimes against the normative event-order model before extending the complete cost-model claim. This case is not covered by the current positive-duration aggregation witnesses.

title: Complete source oracle/lproc binding and advanced scheduler realisations after ref contract repair
description: Known postponed algorithms, never a generic unsupported fallback: §3.6/§3.7 source state/frame and fixed-instance descriptors; §11 K55 staged literal-budget domains; K65/K80/K81 whole-pair recompute with joint-version source partition; qinplace inverse-pair coverage; qloop-while flags, local qregion restoration, coherent address source bindings. Oracle arithmetic depends on bennett-sched-enz. Track exact unsupported feature diagnostics and matrix/certificate conformance gaps in docs/PLAN.md. Primitive action paths, ABI, costs, selectors and portable vector inventory can proceed independently.
notes:
Deferred algorithms additionally include general non-permutation workspace factorisation/cleanup-window proof and semantic-call workspace cleanup-pair partition. These receive explicit tracked UNSUPPORTED responses rather than assuming that syntactic primitive cancellation proves clean release. Source primitive copy/XOR/exchange, native gates, plain loops, qif and exact target schemes are implemented. Full oracle/lproc binding and rigorous certificate replay remain open. Conformance inventory: 519 published cases, 10 normative objects, four portable manifests; report distinguishes direct/equivalent test coverage from all unexercised vectors.
Context-varying certificate frame descriptors (same closure invoked on different resolved classes or workspace shapes) are also explicitly deferred. A regression requires UNSUPPORTED with the named feature instead of emitting the first context frame as if it covered every invocation. Full general cleanup-window proof, imported-model quantity conversion and rigorous claim replay remain outside the implemented cost/action slice.
A source regression reproduced an unsafe acceptance when a qcopy input was permuted and restored while its workspace changed. Supported primitive cleanup now requires stable workspace input dependencies; cases needing the broader §6.2 mutable-version window proof return the specific tracked UNSUPPORTED reason. This preserves the window obligation rather than equating net primitive cancellation with source validity.
